name: Shang
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Blench, Roger. 2010. The Shang language of Central Nigeria and its affinities [annotated Shang wordlist, collected at Kushampa 11 May 2009]. Draft circulated for comment, printout August 31, 2010. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 23 pp.
catalog_locator: sec. 1 Introduction (p. 1), sec. 3 Phonology and 3.3 Tones (pp. 1-2), sec. 4.1 Nouns (p. 2); saved
catalog_quote: The wordlist was collected as a ‘one-shot’ exercise and the transcription must therefore be regarded as preliminary. [...] 3. Phonology The phonology of Shang should be regarded as tentative. [...] 3.3 Tones Shang appears to have three level tones, plus a falling tone. In this transcription, mid tone is left unmarked. Tones are marked as follows; High ˊ Mid Unmarked Low ˋ Rising ˇ Falling ˆ [...] 4.1 Nouns [...] The tone on the vowel of the plural affix always appears to be low tone.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

The quoted passage is there verbatim: 'The phonology of Shang should be regarded as tentative.' opens sec. 3 Phonology (printed p. 1 = PDF page 3), and 'Shang appears to have three level tones, plus a falling tone. In this transcription, mid tone is left unmarked. Tones are marked as follows; High ˊ / Mid Unmarked / Low ˋ / Rising ˇ / Falling ˆ' is sec. 3.3 Tones on printed p. 2 = PDF page 4 (checked with extracted text). Only minor difference: the compiler spliced quote spans pp. 1-2 while the locator names p. 2 alone; the '[..]' marks the splice honestly. a f…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Shang is described as a register-tone language (three level tones plus a falling tone, with a rising tone in the transcription key). The only phonological description in existence (a one-shot wordlist draft) says nothing about word stress or accent; no stress placement rule can be stated.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the author flags the whole phonology as tentative and the transcription as preliminary
new_statements.domain_note: Citation-form wordlist items (233 entries) and nominal plurals; no phrase-level prosody discussed.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Shang of Kushampa A/B (Kagarko LGA, Kaduna State), autonym ù-ʃàŋ pl. àʃaŋ, language ʃàŋ; Glottolog shan1278, no ISO code, absent from Ethnologue. Decker et al. 2021 treat it as a related but distinct language from Zhire (zhir1238, ISO zhi; 43-61% lexical similarity), while Wikipedia (citing Blench 2025) calls it relexified Zhire. Not to be confused with Shanga/Shonga (Mande, Kebbi State) or Sheni (Kainji).

sources.note: Sec. 3 Phonology (pp. 1-2, 'should be regarded as tentative'): 8 oral + 3 marginal nasal vowels, consonant chart, 3.3 Tones p. 2: 'Shang appears to have three level tones, plus a falling tone' (tone-mark table adds a rising mark). No mention of stress or accent anywhere in the document (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Zhire language' (revision downloaded 2026-09-17; 'Shang language' redirects here): 'A variety called Shang is relexified Zhire', citing Blench 2025 'Aspects of the grammar of Zhire [zhi]' (academia.edu) and Hayab 2016 Basic Hyam Grammar
sources.note: Nothing on phonology; useful only as a pointer to Blench 2025 (Zhire grammar) and the SIL survey report.

sources.citation: Decker, Ken, Julius Dabet, John Muniru, Benard Abraham & Innocent Jonah. 2021. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Zhire [zhi] Language of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2021-008. Dallas: SIL International. 51 pp.
sources.note: Sec. 6.5 'Comparison with Shang' pp. 15-16 reproduces Blench 2010's Shang consonant and vowel inventories (tables 12-13) and says 'Blench (2010) also notes five tones: high [á], low [à], rising [ǎ], falling [â], and an unmarked mid tone, which is like what we found in Zhire' (p. 16). Zhire phonology sketch (sec. 6.1-6.4, pp. 8-15) is tentative, 'no in-depth analysis of tones'. No statement on stress/accent for Shang or Zhire (a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing).
